fixture_name: Milltown Park toucan-crossing VRU conflicts — real Irish Stage 1 RSA incl. rejected recommendation (ABP 322160)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Constrained shared space at a toucan crossing caused by narrow footpath plus signal-pole/lighting-column obstructions is a recognised cyclist–pedestrian conflict mechanism with clear preliminary-design relevance.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal claim is anchored by a verbatim quote in EV-IN-025 recording the narrow footpath, both obstructions and the collision potential; nothing beyond the recorded condition is asserted.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly filed as a safety_concern with null normative basis, keeping the collision-risk observation categorically distinct from any compliance question under the PIARC international baseline.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable — relocate the named lighting column and consolidate to single-set signal heads — both viable and appropriate at preliminary design stage, and not a null recommendation.
justifications.vru_coverage: Vulnerable-user impact is central to the finding, explicitly naming pedestrians and cyclists and the collision potential between them.

justifications.substance: Shared-use width inadequacy creating pedestrian-cyclist collision risk is a substantive, scheme-relevant safety concern at preliminary design stage.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal insufficiency-and-collision claim is supported by a verbatim quote in EV-IN-026, exceeding the registry-id-only cap; rejection history is correctly quarantined as provenance.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Framed strictly as a safety concern under the PIARC-derived international baseline with no compliance conflation and no fabricated normative basis.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable (named approach, widen action) and viable at preliminary design; cited physical constraints sit in reviewer_note, not the judged substance.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are the explicit subject of the finding and their mutual collision interaction is directly considered.
